disease_label_per_paper: Biopsy-proven giant cell arteritis with simultaneous bilateral posterior ischemic optic neuropathy
presentation_summary: 80-year-old hypertensive and diabetic man was referred after sudden bilateral painless visual loss five days earlier.
He had a year-long history of bilateral temporal headache, more prominent on the left; frequency increased to almost daily in the months before vision loss.
He had no previous diplopia, transient visual loss, jaw claudication, myalgia, constitutional symptoms, motor symptoms, or sensory symptoms.
Examination showed normal blood pressure, heart rate, and temperature; no light perception in both eyes with bilaterally dilated nonreactive pupils and normal fundus exam.
CRP was 132 mg/L and ESR was 40 mm/hr. MRI/MRA showed right optic nerve ischemia and absent bilateral ophthalmic artery flow; temporal artery biopsy confirmed GCA.
